title: Tears of Steel: The Bridge
synopsis: On a canal bridge in Amsterdam, Celia tells Thom he's a jerk. He talks about following his passions, she asks if he is scared of her robot hand, and the argument ends with a cold goodbye.

characters.description: Wants to be awesome in space and is not great at saying sorry.
Works in robotics and is done with Thom's excuses.

lines.text: Look Celia, we have to follow our passions;
you have your robotics, and I just want to be awesome in space.
Why don't you just admit that you're freaked out by my robot hand?
I'm not freaked out by— it's...
I'm freaked out! I have nightmares that I'm being chased...
by these giant robotic claws of death.

This scene is an excerpt of the film, trimmed and re-encoded, with its dialogue and background audio rebuilt from the official 5.1 center channel and music and effects mix.
modifications: Trimmed the 720p release (tears_of_steel_720p.mov) to 22.500-45.500 s and re-encoded video as H.264 and audio as AAC-LC at 48 kHz.

Dialogue tracks: the official 5.1 center channel (TOS_DVDSURROUND.C.aif), trimmed to the same range, gated per character to that character's line windows with 10 ms fades, silent elsewhere, encoded as dual-mono AAC-LC.
Background track: the official music and effects mix without dialogue (TOS_MUSIC+FX_NO_DIALOGUE.aif), trimmed to the same range and encoded as AAC-LC.
Poster: a single frame extracted from the trimmed video.

Line windows were set from speech energy in the center channel. Wording follows the official English subtitles (TOS-en.srt), lightly normalized, and was cross-checked with a speech recognizer, not by ear.

dialogueSeparation.tool: Official Blender Foundation release files; no model separation. dialogueSeparation.notes: Dialogue is the 5.1 center channel, which carries the speech in this scene but is not a certified dry dialogue stem. The film's stereo mix, 5.1 mix and music-and-effects file are separate renders, so background plus dialogue reproduces the video's own audio only approximately: per-line waveform correlation of the dialogue tracks with the video audio is 0.4 to 0.7, the center channel runs about 6 ms behind the video audio before the 40.25 s picture cut and about 18 ms ahead after it, and the music-and-effects file only loosely matches the mix outside the dialogue. The background keeps the film's score by Joram Letwory (about 22.5 to 25 s and from about 40.4 s). The film is released under CC BY 3.0, but the composer's separately released Original Soundtrack files are CC BY-ND, and he asks anyone who cuts up the music to contact him first. Whether this background excerpt needs that permission is unresolved. See docs/demo-scenes.md.
